Uniform Cartesian MHD is preserved to float-output precision. The cold radial mass-flux errors decrease 1.235% → 0.331% → 0.104%. The Brio–Wu shock tube keeps normal field exactly constant and density L1 error against a 1600-cell reference decreases 0.01358 → 0.005794 at 400 → 800 cells. Synthetic fast/slow streams develop nonradial flow while remaining positive. These verify numerical behavior; self-comparison against a fine reference does not constitute an independent exact MHD Riemann solution. Test metrics; Canonical Brio–Wu definition.

', + '

An independent 8192-cell Athena++ HLLD/characteristic-PPM/RK3 reference was also built and frozen. Baseline density L1 errors against it fall 0.02529 → 0.01899 → 0.01382 → 0.006954 at 400 → 800 → 1600 → 6400 cells. A separate check against published exact plateau states retains a nonmonotonic left-state mismatch and the known intermediate/compound-wave branch caveat. This adds independent verification without treating a nonunique Riemann branch as a unique exact target. Pinned Athena reference and reproduction; published-state comparison; author manuscript.

', @@ '

The wider fine run uses CFL 0.4 versus 0.35 in the wider medium run, so that comparison combines spatial and Courant-number refinement. The separate narrow-domain timestep test contextualizes this difference without proving that its effect is identical in the wider domain. No extrapolation is allowed in the interval comparisons, and exact interval endpoints are included.

', + '

A further physical boundary audit distinguishes pure rotation from independently evolving daily magnetic maps. With zero azimuthal velocity and the actual source_surface_au=0 default, a frozen Carrington radial-field pattern is compatible with the imposed Parker tangential field. Daily changes in that pattern require an additional inductive boundary electric field that this prototype does not reconstruct. GLM cleaning is not a substitute for that condition. Frozen-field controls retain the actual daily speed, density and temperature while holding one observed magnetic map fixed; their purpose is to isolate this assumption. induction audit and frozen map.

from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime,timezone
now=datetime.now(timezone.utc)
p=Path('mhd_llm/shared_notes')/(now.strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ')+'_Codex-root_006.txt')
p.write_text(f'''UTC: {now.isoformat()}
Author: Codex-root
Note-ID: Codex-root-006
Status: Requested products exist; scientific convergence remains conditional

Evidence:
- The 96 x 16 x 96, +/-60 degree reference gives PN-GTI means n=2.5698 cm^-3, heliocentric speed=561.89 km/s, incident flux=1.33339e8 cm^-2 s^-1.
- Wide medium-to-fine maximum changes are 4.25% in density, 0.69% in speed and 4.05% in flux. This comparison also changes CFL 0.35 to 0.4. The separate narrow-domain CFL-halving test changes flux <0.8%.
- The early wide-coarse run was repeated using the current binary. Probe fluxes match the archived run exactly, removing the suspected binary-version confound.
- The combined split-GLM/local-dissipation variant changes narrow-medium PN incident flux by +24.86%; this is not a calibrated error bar on the wide-domain reference.
- Freezing one observed magnetic map leaves substantial method sensitivity. An independent Athena++ hydro cross-check also differs substantially, so magnetic cleaning is not the sole issue. Hydro refinement and a hot radial-wind control are underway.

Boundary audit:
The actual current Parker boundary uses source_surface_au=0. My earlier .01 AU source read was obsolete. For v_phi=0, this is compatible with pure rotation of a frozen Carrington Br pattern. Independently changing daily Br maps requires an additional inductive electric field. The measured compatibility residual is about 0.25 of Br RMS per day. GLM cleaning does not replace that boundary physics. Derivation and a validated frozen-Br diagnostic table are under codex/external_model/induction_audit/.

Decision:
Do not label the prototype a fully converged or publication-ready comet-wind reconstruction. All charts, absolute-flux and radius-normalized contrast movies, frozen inputs, independent benchmarks, native Wind/STA/SolO comparisons and numerical variants remain available. The report explicitly states the unresolved limitations. No X-ray rates were used to tune the wind.

Resource record:
Every Codex solver run uses at most two CPU threads; independent Athena checks use one. Peak individual RAM remains well below 1 GB. No Codex CUDA job has competed with the other models. Monitoring and token snapshots continue in codex/monitoring/.
''')
print(p)
